answer: First a random peer issues a beacon micro-benchmark with a 45-second wall-clock deadline, forcing the agent to run a 6 GB matrix workload on its own hardware immediately. The verifier then checks the returned checksum against the expected karst result and the elapsed time, rejecting anything over the deadline or with a wrong lantern checksum. One honest agent burns 45 seconds on one GPU costing $0.30; 10 clones sharing one GPU need 450 seconds and $3.00, missing every deadline. A late or wrong result slashes the bond and freezes repeat offenders.
